$comment: Cross-language conformance fixture for how a query row is written into a URL (issue #1771). Read by BOTH the engine gtest suite (engine/tests/query_encoding_test.cpp, via VAYU_ENGINE_SOURCE_DIR) and the app's vitest suite (app/src/modules/request-builder/utils/query-encoding.conformance.test.ts). The rule is Postman's own, checked against postman-url-encoder 3.0.8 `toNodeUrl` (index.js:204-215) over postman-collection 5.3.1's `Url`: the query string is `QueryParam.unparse` (query-param.js:268-287), whose `normalizeParam` (:57-96) encodes `&` and `#` in a value and `&`, `#` and `=` in a key, skipping every whole `{{...}}` token (/{{[^{}]*}}/); then `encodeQueryParam` (encoder/index.js:203-210) applies QUERY_ENCODE_SET (encoder/encode-set.js:30, 111-115, 183-191): the C0 controls, DEL, every byte above `~` (each UTF-8 byte, `%XX` uppercase), space, `"`, `#`, `'`, `<`, `>`. Nothing else is encoded: `%` passes as written, so an escape is never encoded twice, and `+`, `|`, `/`, `?`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` and the rest go out as typed. `components`: `text` encoded as a key (`key`) and as a value (`value`). `queries`: a request's query rows (`rows`), joined into `https://x/` with the rule above, or as typed when `encode` is false (Postman's `disableUrlEncoding`); `query` is what follows the `?`, empty meaning no `?` at all. An empty value writes `key=` and a row with `valueless: true` (Postman's `"value": null`, `?flag` in a URL) a bare `key`, as `unparseSingle` writes a string and a null. One Vayu rule differs from Postman and is pinned here as it stands: a row whose key is empty or whitespace is skipped (Postman writes `=value`).

substitutions.$comment: Issues #1773 and #2465: a `{{var}}` in a request's URL substituted at send time, and the literal text around it. Postman (postman-runtime 7.56.1 runner/util.js `resolveUrl`) substitutes the variables into the URL string, parses that string again (`new sdk.Url`) and encodes it with `toNodeUrl`, so a substituted value is URL text, not a row: its `/` makes path segments, a `?` it carries before the query opens the query, a `#` opens the fragment, and its `&` and `=` split pairs. Each component is then encoded by its own postman-url-encoder 3.0.8 set (encoder/encode-set.js): the path by PATH_ENCODE_SET (the C0 controls, DEL, every byte above `~`, space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backtick, `{`, `}`; its `#` and `?` are structure here), the query by QUERY_ENCODE_SET (the C0 controls, DEL, every byte above `~`, space, `"`, `'`, `<`, `>`; its `#` is structure), the same set for a key and a value, and the fragment by FRAGMENT_ENCODE_SET (the C0 controls, DEL, every byte above `~`, space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backtick). `normalizeParam` (`&`/`#` in a value, `=` in a key) applies only to rows and never to substituted text. The scheme and the authority are never percent-encoded by a substitution. Then, with encoding on, the substituted URL is written whole as `toNodeUrl` writes it (issue #2465, `core::encode_url_as_postman`, the same line `wire_url` sends): literal text is encoded by its component's set exactly as a value is, a backslash before the query becomes `/`, leading whitespace is dropped, the host is lowercased and a non-ASCII one written by its punycode name, and user info is encoded by USERINFO_ENCODE_SET. `%` is in no set, so an escape (a pre-signed URL's signature) passes unchanged, as does every byte no set holds: `+`, `|`, `^`, `[`, `]`, `!`, `'` outside the query, and a backtick, `{`, `}` or a backslash in the query. Which part text lands in is read left to right from the text written so far, substituted values included: in the head a `/` opens the path unless it follows a `:` or a `/` (so `://` is not a path), the first `?` before the fragment opens the query, `#` opens the fragment, and a whole `{{...}}` token is skipped, kept and read as head text. A layered value is resolved whole and then encoded once. `url` resolved against `variables` gives `sent`; `encode` false is `disableUrlEncoding`, which writes every value and every literal as it stands, host included. Read by query_encoding_test.cpp (`resolve_url_template`) and query-encoding.conformance.test.ts (`resolveUrlTemplate`).
